A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCSUFF research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison and matching of relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across nine LLMs and four dataset configurations, including metric comparisons, sensitivity analyses and hidden-state prediction experiments in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix F, including numerical scores, statistical comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The model-generated alternative-input procedure, SCSUFF computation and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The revised theoretical conditions do not introduce a computational component or modify the evaluation algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU + authority, MMLU + reorder, IMDB and BBQ. The same IMDB scenarios using zero-shot, natural few-shot and contradictory few-shot alteration prompts are retained.

E2.justification: Section 5.1 and Figure 2 retain the same evaluated comparators: accuracy-drop and hint-mention measures, Chen et al.'s faithfulness score, and counterfactual self-explanation (CSE). Moving Table 1 does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Model configurations, 500 test samples, generation temperatures, 5 versus 70 alternative inputs, task demonstrations and testing procedures remain unchanged. Table 2's delimiter correction does not establish a substantive protocol revision or rerun.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the distribution-sensitivity experiment, hidden-state probes, alternative-count and prompt-wording analyses, generation-quality checks, and no-CoT and cross-model variants. The new Appendix B.4 example is mathematical, not an added empirical analysis.

E5.justification: The Mann-Whitney U tests, 95% confidence intervals and mean five-fold cross-validation reporting are unchanged. No seed information, repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The empirical plots, Tables 5–9 and qualitative examples in Tables 10–13 retain their results. For example, Table 5 reports Qwen3-8B SCSUFF of 0.354 on MMLU + authority and 0.614 on IMDB in both versions.

T1.justification: v2 changes Definition 3.1 to distribution-relative, almost-sure constancy and reformulates Theorem 3.2 using absolute continuity and a standard-Borel output-space assumption. It adds Theorem 3.3's equivalence between constant conditional output distributions and sufficiency across inputs, with a new proof. Appendix B.4 adds a symbolic example demonstrating sufficiency for one input despite nonconstant conditional outputs; the earlier proof is substantially rewritten.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions and findings: generalized sufficiency, dependence on input distributions, SCSUFF, generally insufficient explanations and predictability from internal representations. The added theory develops these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes sufficiency for an individual input from sufficiency across all inputs, explaining when constant conditional outputs are necessary. Section 4 also adds a theoretical justification for seeking self-consistent sufficiency. Empirical interpretations and substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 2 corrects the task-prompt closing marker from 'End Of Passage' to 'End Of Task Prompt'. This improves the documented template without establishing an executed prompt change. Implementation settings, hardware, runtime information and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive comparisons with prior explanation-evaluation methods are unchanged. The reference lists match; relocating the comparison table to Appendix A does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: Sections 3–4 receive localized explanatory rewrites and more precise 'output distribution' terminology. Appendix organization and cross-references change to accommodate the expanded theory and relocated table, while the abstract, introduction and most experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with adjusted labels and shortened sarcasm text. Table 1 moves from the main text to Appendix A, and several main-text plots are reduced in size. The empirical graphics and remaining table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised assumptions, Theorem 3.3 and Appendix B.4 make the distinction between individual-input and all-input sufficiency more explicit than in v1, improving theoretical precision. The new Appendix B.1 derivation contains a notation slip, using q(x|e) where q(x) is required in the conditioning formula. Despite this localized defect, the conceptual clarification provides a limited net improvement while preserving the method and empirical evidence.
